newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Decision near on Portugal pulp restructuring - paper.
newsitem.headline: Decision near on Portugal pulp restructuring - paper.

text.p: The Portuguese Economy Ministry's two scenarios for the national pulp and paper industry involve the merging of Portucel Industrial and Soporcel but exclude Inapa, the Publico newspaper said on Wednesday.
A final decision could be taken next week with the ministry announcing the plan by the end of the month, it said without giving a source.
The paper said that one of the plans called for state-owned savings bank CGD-Caixa Geral de Depositos and Arjo Wiggins, which control Soporcel, to exchange their holdings for shares in Portucel.

The other would involve the launching of a buyout by Portucel, which would at the same time increase its share capital, with a prior accord with the Soporcel shareholders that they would take stakes in the pulp group.
The newspaper gave no further details.
The state has a 60 percent direct stake in Portucel, whereas state-owned Caixa has 51 percent of Soporcel.
The same article quoted Soporcel chairman Alvaro Barreto as saying the scenarios were "pure speculation". Economy Minister Augusto Mateus declined to comment, it added.
